item.title: FIRST ON FOX: ICE quietly arrests jaw dropping number of illegal immigrants in massive DC area operation
item.description: U.S. ICE arrested 1,328 illegal immigrants in Virginia and Maryland in just 14 days, including a Salvadoran alien wanted on a murder warrant.
item.content:encoded:

Multiple ICE sources told Fox News that the agency arrested 1,328 illegal immigrants over 14 days in the Washington, D.C., suburbs. The arrests took place in Virginia and Maryland, both of which have sanctuary-type policies in place.

Of those arrested, almost 400 illegal immigrants had criminal convictions or pending criminal charges, including a Salvadoran national wanted in Richmond, Virginia, on a murder warrant. Other crimes included rape, sexual assault, kidnapping, DUI, robbery and attempted murder.

The operation comes as Maryland and Virginia, particularly Fairfax County, Virginia, have seen significant crime involving illegal immigrants, including violent and sexual offenses.

The operation, titled "Operation Safe Community — Washington, D.C.," took place from Aug. 1-14.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told Fox News that "the brave men and women of ICE are hard at work every single day getting these dangerous illegal aliens out of our country."

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S IMMIGRATION PUSH FUELS ICE'S BIGGEST ARREST MONTH IN AGENCY HISTORY

Mullin added that "while sanctuary politicians in Virginia and Maryland keep putting the needs of illegal aliens over the safety of the American people, the Trump Administration will always put American citizens first."

item.title: Missouri assistant fire chief charged with murder after hidden video found on wife's phone, investigators say
item.description: A hidden phone video and forensic blood spatter analysis unraveled Jeremy Perrien's claim that his wife Shelby Perrien shot herself during a drive, authorities say.
item.content:encoded:
Content warning: This article contains references to domestic abuse that some readers may find distressing.

A Missouri assistant fire chief who spent over a year claiming his wife killed herself while they were driving down the highway was slapped with murder charges after a hidden phone video blew his cover, investigators say.

Jeremy Perrien, 45, was arrested Friday, Aug. 21, at Fire Station Four in Scott County, Missouri, bringing an end to a 14-month investigation in the small town. He was charged with second-degree murder, felony harassment, domestic assault and two counts of tampering with physical evidence in a felony prosecution.

According to an affidavit reviewed by Fox News Digital, the assistant fire chief initially told authorities that he and his wife, 31-year-old Shelby Perrien, were driving back from a bar in Cape Girardeau on June 25, 2025, when she said, "I'm sorry, I'm a piece of s---," pulled out a .380 caliber handgun and shot herself in the head.

But investigators now say his story was a sham and that behind closed doors, the assistant fire chief was allegedly living a double life.

DISPATCH AUDIO REVEALS WHAT WAS HEARD INSIDE JOSH JACOBS' HOME BEFORE ALLEGED DOMESTIC VIOLENCE ARREST

When detectives cracked open Shelby's cellphone, they unlocked a "hidden folder" containing a 90-second video recorded just a month before her death. In the video, according to the affidavit, Jeremy was seen striking his wife, grabbing her by the throat, choking her and repeatedly punching her. Investigators said Perrien also threatened to kill her multiple times during the recording.

"I would not get mouthy with me. I will, I’ll f------. I want to kill you so f------ bad right now," Jeremy allegedly told his wife.

"If you’re going to lie, then I’m just going to smash your face and go to jail and end my f------ life with you," he allegedly said.

At another point in the graphic exchange, Jeremy allegedly threw his wedding band in her face and said, "I'm never wearing that son a b---- again."

State police also recovered disturbing text messages where Jeremy allegedly sent: "You 100% will need a body bag if I stay with you. Each time my rage is worse."

In another message, according to the affidavit, he wrote, "I'd be lying to you if I told you that I was hoping that you wouldn't commit suicide."

Perrien's undoing came from the crime lab after forensic analysis of the blood spatter and physical evidence inside the vehicle determined it was impossible for Shelby to have pulled the trigger, according to authorities.

item.title: Card skimming scam is stealing food benefits nationwide
item.description: A single card skimmer can generate $1 million in stolen funds, and Secret Service video shows criminals installing them in under two seconds.
item.content:encoded:
You swipe your card at the checkout, grab your receipt and walk away. Nothing looks unusual. However, a device sitting right on top of that payment terminal may have copied your card information and PIN.

U.S. Secret Service agents recently swept hundreds of retailers across Los Angeles looking for skimmers. What they found shows how sophisticated these devices have become and how difficult they can be to spot.

This card skimming scam is especially serious for people who rely on Electronic Benefit Transfer, or EBT, cards. Many of those cards still depend on magnetic-stripe technology that criminals know how to exploit.

INSIDE NYC'S 'PERFECT SCAM': LUXURY CARS, DUSTY SHELVES AND THE EBT SECRET BEHIND THE COUNTER

New! Free live CyberGuy class: Protect Your Money From Today’s Biggest Threats

Join us Saturday, Aug. 29, at 10 a.m. ET for a free CyberGuy LIVE class covering five simple steps to help defend yourself against AI scams, fraud, identity theft and financial hacks. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson will explain how to set up bank alerts, strengthen your account logins, protect your phone number, freeze your credit and help secure your retirement savings against unauthorized transfers. No technical experience is needed. You’ll also receive our financial protection checklist, and every registrant will get a link to the class recording afterward.

Reserve your free spot today at CyberGuyLive.com.

One of the most unsettling parts of the investigation is how quickly criminals can install a skimmer. Surveillance video from the investigation captured a suspect placing one over a payment terminal in less than two seconds. From there, the fake reader sits directly over the real terminal. When someone swipes a card, the device can capture account information and the PIN used during the transaction.

We have previously shown you how skimmers and shimmers can steal your payment information. What stands out now is how convincing these newer devices can look. During the Secret Service sweep, agents found a skimmer that blended closely into the legitimate payment terminal. It even had what appeared to be a security hologram.

Agents had to pry the device off. Inside, they found miniature electronics and a wireless transmitter. That transmitter can send stolen information to a criminal nearby. The person who installed the skimmer may not have to return and remove it to collect the data.

The numbers behind this crime are staggering. The Secret Service says a single skimmer can generate as much as $1 million in stolen funds.

Across the country, 32 active federal investigations span 15 states. Meanwhile, the Secret Service estimates that skimming costs consumers and financial institutions more than $1 billion each year.

The agency has also stepped up its nationwide enforcement efforts. During 2025 operations, law enforcement removed more than 400 illegal skimming devices. The Secret Service says skimming activity has increasingly targeted EBT cards.

A recent Los Angeles sweep shows how widespread the problem has become. Law enforcement visited 328 businesses and inspected 1,749 payment devices. Agents seized 16 skimmers. The Secret Service estimated those removals prevented about $16.6 million in potential fraud losses.

This is where things take a troubling turn. The Secret Service says criminals intentionally target locations with heavy EBT use. That includes stores where people use government benefits to buy groceries.

Many credit and debit cards now offer chips or contactless payment. However, many EBT transactions still require a magnetic-stripe swipe. That gives criminals an opening. A skimmer can capture the information stored on the magnetic stripe. Criminals can then copy that information onto another magnetic-stripe card. If they also capture the victim's PIN, they can use the cloned card to steal benefits.

For people who rely on those benefits, the impact can be immediate. Victims may discover their accounts have been drained when they try to buy groceries or pay for everyday necessities. Recovering stolen benefits can also take time, leaving families without money they were counting on.

VENEZUELAN NATIONALS CHARGED IN $529K ATM JACKPOTTING SCHEME AT I-95 REST STOPS, FEDS SAY

Federal officials know the magnetic stripe is a weak point. The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food and Nutrition Service says EBT fraud involving skimming is rising. The agency is working with states on modernizing SNAP EBT systems, including introducing chip cards.

Chip technology makes card information harder to copy than data stored on a magnetic stripe. Still, that transition takes time. Until more EBT systems support newer payment technology, millions of people may continue using cards that require a swipe. That leaves benefit recipients with fewer ways to avoid the very payment method criminals are targeting.

The Secret Service says organized criminal groups are involved in some of these skimming schemes. Investigators have linked some operations to groups that travel into the United States and move between locations installing devices.

The agency has been conducting skimming operations across the country throughout 2026. Recent sweeps have focused on payment terminals at stores and ATMs where skimming activity is suspected. That kind of coordinated activity can make the devices harder to track and allow criminals to target multiple locations in a short period of time.

You may never spot a well-made skimmer by sight alone. Still, you can lower your risk and catch suspicious activity faster.

If a payment terminal supports contactless payments, use them. The Secret Service recommends tap-to-pay when possible. You can also use a digital wallet on your phone if the retailer supports it. For more ways to protect your cards in stores and online, see our guide on how to protect your credit and bank cards from getting hacked.

Take a few seconds before inserting or swiping your card. Look for a reader that appears loose or crooked. Also watch for damage, unusual gaps or parts that do not seem to line up correctly. The Secret Service recommends avoiding a reader if something looks altered or damaged.

IDENTITY THEFT RARELY ANNOUNCES ITSELF: 6 SIGNS YOU MISSED

Some overlay skimmers sit directly on top of the legitimate card reader. Before swiping, gently check whether anything feels loose or moves unexpectedly. Do not try to rip apart a terminal. If something seems suspicious, stop using it and notify the store.

A skimmer may capture card information while another device records your PIN. Use your hand to shield the keypad whenever you enter a PIN. That simple habit can make captured card information less useful to a criminal.

Enable alerts through your bank or card issuer so you know when your card gets used. Pay attention to small charges too. If you see something you do not recognize, contact your financial institution using the number on your card or its official app. If money has already disappeared from an account, follow our steps on what to do if your bank account is hacked.

EBT users should review their account history for transactions they do not recognize. The Food and Nutrition Service recommends checking EBT accounts regularly. It also advises changing your PIN at least once a month, particularly before your benefits are issued. If you spot an unauthorized transaction, change your PIN immediately and contact your state EBT agency.

Government agencies should not need your PIN to verify your eligibility. Do not provide your EBT card number or PIN in response to an unexpected text, phone call or email. Federal officials warn that criminals use several methods to steal benefit information, so protecting the PIN remains important even when no physical skimmer is involved.

Act quickly once you notice suspicious transactions.

What bothers me most about this scam is that criminals are going after people who may have the fewest options to protect themselves. If I can tap my credit card or pay with my phone, I can avoid swiping altogether. Many EBT users cannot make that same choice because their cards still rely on older magnetic-stripe technology. That needs to change. These skimmers have become convincing enough to fool almost anyone, and some can transmit stolen information without the criminal ever coming back for the device. You can check the reader and keep an eye on your account, but there is only so much you can do when the payment system itself leaves you exposed. Moving benefit cards to more secure technology should be a priority, especially when families are depending on that money for food.

item.title: Tourists smash SUV window to free black bear trapped inside their vehicle in Gatlinburg
item.description: Video shows tourists in Gatlinburg smashing an SUV's rear window with a large rock to free a trapped black bear near Great Smoky Mountains National Park.
item.content:encoded:
A group of tourists in Tennessee went to some pretty extreme lengths last week to rescue a black bear that had gotten itself locked inside their SUV.

Video of the chaotic scene shows the bear moving around inside the vehicle while the group tries to figure out how to get it out. One man first attempts to use what appears to be a Slim Jim tool to unlock one of the front doors from the outside.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

No luck. So they moved on to Plan B: sacrifice the window.

Another man grabbed a large rock and smashed out the rear window of the SUV. Once the glass shattered, all three people immediately took off running for dear life.

Seconds later, the huge bear crawled through the broken window and made its escape.

The incident, which was captured on video, happened in Gatlinburg, where encounters between people and black bears are pretty much a daily occurrence during warmer months. Great Smoky Mountains National Park is home to approximately 1,900 American black bears and sees around 12 million visitors each year.

It was not clear exactly how the bear got into the SUV, but it was likely looking for food when it accidentally locked itself inside. And apparently, the keys got locked inside with the animal.

All things considered, this was a happy ending for the bear. It doesn’t always work out that way.

Earlier this month, Colorado Parks and Wildlife reported that a black bear died after getting trapped inside an unlocked vehicle in Colorado Springs. The bear apparently opened the vehicle door, climbed inside and then became trapped when the door closed behind it.

The animal tore apart the interior while trying to escape but was not discovered for several days.

Colorado Parks and Wildlife officer Travis Sauder told The Colorado Springs Gazette that bears are more than capable of getting themselves into vehicles — getting back out can be the problem.

"Typically what happens is they pull the door open, get in, get their food, and then they leave," Sauder said. "But sometimes the door closes behind them and they have trouble figuring out how to get out."

A PRACTICAL GUIDE TO NOT GETTING MAULED BY A BEAR WHILE HIKING OR CAMPING THIS SUMMER

That wasn't even the only recent case in Colorado.

On July 29, another black bear got inside an unlocked vehicle in Manitou Springs and spent hours trapped inside, destroying much of the interior as it tried to escape. Firefighters eventually freed the bear, which escaped into nearby Pike National Forest before wildlife officials could relocate it.

But it’s best for everyone involved (humans, bears and cars) to avoid this situation altogether.

The National Park Service specifically warns visitors in the Smoky Mountains to lock their vehicles and not to leave food, garbage or other scented items inside.

And — as these folks in Gatlinburg learned the hard way — maybe double-check that your keys aren’t in there, either.

ISRAELI POLICE SAY IRAN USING WHATSAPP, FACEBOOK, BLACKMAIL TO RECRUIT SPIES AS LATEST ATTEMPT FOILED

item.title: Vance says Canada friendlier to China on trade than to US: 'Insanity'
item.description: JD Vance told Maine voters that Canada treats Chinese goods more fairly than Maine farm products, blaming Ottawa for derailing trade talks.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump's trade talks with Canada have stalled – with threats of retaliatory tariffs ramping up again – but Vice President JD Vance was in Maine, explaining to voters that Canada has been friendlier to China on trade than to them, particularly farmers.

"They treat Chinese goods more fairly than they do the goods that come from the people of Maine: It’s insanity," Vance said during a question-and-answer session in Brewer, Maine, on Monday afternoon. "And what we’ve said to Canada is stop it."

Vance said he believes the U.S. and Canada had been close to reaching a trade agreement before negotiations broke down, blaming Ottawa for bringing what he described as "unreasonable last-minute demands" to the table.

TRUMP TRADE CHIEF WARNS CANADA WALKED AWAY FROM 'THE BEST DEAL' TO TRIGGER 50% U.S. TARIFFS

"I frankly thought we had a deal," Vance said. "I think that we should have a deal, but I think that we need to send a message loud and clear to the prime minister of Canada: Stop taking advantage of the people of Maine. Stop taking advantage of America. It’s over."

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced Friday that Canada was suspending negotiations. Trump posted Monday on Truth Social that he plans to impose 50% tariffs on Canadian-made vehicles, auto parts and steel beginning in January 2027.

"Canada has been ripping off the United States of America for years," Trump wrote. "Their ridiculously high tariffs on our Farmers and farm products has made life impossible for these great American Patriots, and has long created a 60 Billion Dollar Deficit between our two Countries. Not sustainable, and NOT ANYMORE!"

TRUMP ALLIES PUSH TO ARM PRESIDENT WITH NEW TARIFF WEAPON TO PUNISH COUNTRIES 'RIPPING OFF' AMERICA

Vance made the remarks during an appearance at Compotech, a defense technology manufacturer in Brewer, as the vice president fielded a question about how the administration’s tariffs could affect Maine businesses and consumers.

"We’re very mindful of the fact that Maine is a border state with Canada," Vance said. "There’s a lot of cross-border transaction between Maine and Canada. And what we’re trying to do here is just make sure that Maine actually gets a fair deal."

Vance argued that Canada and China have been among the worst offenders when it comes to trade barriers against the U.S., while drawing a sharp distinction between what Washington expects from an economic competitor and from a longtime ally.

CHAD WOLF: AMERICA CANNOT IGNORE CHINA’S ECONOMIC ATTACK ON US INDUSTRY

"China, you of course expect — they’re our biggest economic competitor," Vance said. "I would expect that from China. I would not expect that from Canada."

Vance then briefly referred to Canada as a "state" before immediately correcting himself, referencing Trump's long-running trolling of Canada, teasing it as the 51st state.

"We have to remember Canada is a state — sorry, Freudian slip — that was actually an accident," Vance said. "Canada is a country that has underinvested in its military that quite literally would get invaded by a foreign country were it not for the umbrella of protection provided by the United States of America."

CHAD WOLF: CANADA CAN'T EXPECT FREE TRADE WHILE LEAVING OUR NORTHERN BORDER VULNERABLE

He argued that Canada had responded to that relationship by imposing trade restrictions on American products while expecting the U.S. not to retaliate.

"They apply ridiculous tariffs and other non-tariff duties on Maine products coming into Canada, and they don’t expect Maine or anybody else to fight back," Vance said. "We’re sick of that."

"We are actually going to fight back against unfair trade practices, whether it’s coming from China or Canada."

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION EXPANDS 'PRODUCT OF USA' LABEL AS PUSH FOR AMERICAN-RAISED BEEF GROWS

Vance pointed specifically to dairy products, contrasting the treatment of Canadian products entering Maine with the tariffs that can apply when U.S. dairy exports exceed Canada’s tariff-rate quotas.

"If a Maine farmer sends dairy products into Canada, they could be paying as much as a 250% tariff," Vance said. "Now, how is it fair to the farmers of Maine that they pay 250% when the Canadian farmers pay nothing?"

CANADA REPORTEDLY SCRAPS JOINT BRIDGE CELEBRATION WITH US AFTER TRUMP RENEWS TARIFF THREAT

Canada’s dairy system provides duty-free access for set quantities of U.S. products under the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement, but steep tariffs can apply once imports exceed those quotas. Canada’s tariff schedule, for example, lists a 241% over-quota rate for certain milk products, while other dairy categories can carry even higher rates.

Vance also accused Canada of allowing Chinese goods to use the country as a route into the North American market, saying that issue had become part of the latest negotiations.

"We know that Canada allows itself to be used as a back door for Chinese goods," Vance said.

Vance nevertheless left open the possibility of the two sides returning to an agreement, even as he made clear the administration was prepared to keep tariffs in place without concessions from Ottawa.

"I think that we should have a deal," Vance said. "We expect fairness in our trade policy."

item.title: Royce White predicts Enes Kanter Freedom will be suspended from WNBA events after run in with Natasha Cloud
item.description: Royce White predicts the WNBA will ban Enes Kanter Freedom from future events after his viral courtside exchange with Natasha Cloud in Chicago.
item.content:encoded:
Former NBA player Royce White believes Enes Kanter Freedom’s removal from a WNBA game following his exchange with Chicago Sky guard Natasha Cloud may be only the beginning of the league’s response.

White, who, like Freedom, has officially declared for the 2027 WNBA Draft to challenge the league's eligibility policies, joined 'Don't @ Me w/ Dan Dakich' on Monday and shared his reaction to the now-viral moment that unfolded in Chicago on Sunday during the Indiana Fever's 113-90 win over the Sky.

During a break in the action in the third quarter, Cloud began talking towards Freedom, who was sitting court side. The former NBA forward responded by stepping toward the floor, leading Cloud to approach him, before security got involved and escorted Freedom out of the arena.

When asked by Dakich whether he believes Freedom may have made a mistake by getting involved with Cloud, White took things in a bit of a different direction, and predicted the WNBA will intervene with authority.

"I just know how the business works and how the PR works, and they're going to say that he instigated a conflict with a player, and there is an immutable line between the spectators and the players," White began.

"They're going to make a statement that he's, you know, indefinitely suspended or banned from WNBA events, if not NBA and WNBA. Same as the guy who was caught throwing the dildo on the court. Now it's a very different deal what that guy did and Enes, but they'll treat it the same because of the nature of the politics and the controversy. In my opinion, that statement is coming in the next couple of days."

SKY COACH PRAISES NATASHA CLOUD AFTER HEATED VERBAL ALTERCATION WITH ENES KANTER FREEDOM

After being escorted out of the arena, Freedom shared his side of what took place on the floor with Cloud.

"Sophie Cunningham shot a three, and I put my hands up to celebrate," Freedom told Jackson Thompson of Fox News Digital. "Literally, a couple possessions later, Natasha came back and started screaming and yelling and said, ‘She’s not gonna sleep with you.’

"And I was like, ‘I am not trying to sleep with her. I’m just here to protect women and support her.’ And then, obviously, after that she started yapping, and she started to walk towards me, and literally I just got up, and then I was like, ‘I’m just here to protect women, and that’s all.’"

ENES KANTER FREEDOM OPENS UP ON CONFRONTATION WITH NATASHA CLOUD THAT LED TO EJECTION, WNBA PURSUIT

WNBA PLAYER NATASHA CLOUD FIRES OFF PRO-TRANS MESSAGE FOLLOWING ALTERCATION WITH ENES KANTER FREEDOM

Freedom also explained that Cloud began using "some very heavy language" towards him, which surprised him given the many young fans seated within shouting distance.

Freedom and White both declared for the 2027 WNBA Draft earlier this month after Fever star Sophie Cunningham received backlash for stating her opinion that women's sports should be exclusive to women. Freedom and White are using the league’s rules to challenge the WNBA to clarify its eligibility standards.

The WNBA’s current collective bargaining agreement states that "only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA." It does not publicly define the term or establish specific eligibility requirements for transgender athletes.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: LA ICE director reveals officers followed home, harassed as police fail to help in sanctuary city
item.description: ICE Los Angeles Field Office Director Thomas Giles reveals how California sanctuary policies force officers into dangerous public confrontations.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE: From agents being followed home and harassed to dealing with riots and local police refusing to assist, ICE Los Angeles Field Office Director Thomas Giles gave Fox News Digital an inside look at the daily risks of conducting operations in one of America’s largest sanctuary cities.

Fox News Digital accompanied Giles and a team of ICE officers on an immigration enforcement operation in the Los Angeles area early Thursday morning. In an interview from inside his vehicle during the operation, Giles emphasized that while "it's not going to shut us down and stop us," California’s sanctuary policies put both his agents and the community at risk.

"The sanctuary policies definitely impact our operations in terms of it'd be a lot easier for us to have that transfer of custody in a secure environment," he explained. "So, what it does for us is it sends our officers out into the community, putting our officers at risk and other community members at risk to go out and try to apprehend this individual."

item.title: Iran-linked hackers suspected in UK power-plant shutdown after alleged Minnesota water attack
item.description: Iran-linked hackers allegedly forced a British power generator offline for four days, weeks after striking over 30 community water systems in Minnesota.
item.content:encoded:
Iran-linked hackers are suspected of forcing a small British power generator offline for four days last month, the latest sign that Tehran-linked cyber activity may be moving from probing vulnerable systems to causing disruptions U.S. officials have long warned about.

Iran-linked hackers were behind the outage, according to British security officials who spoke with multiple news outlets.

"To be clear: there was no threat to the wider grid and nobody lost power. We have one of the most resilient energy systems in the world," UK Energy Minister Michael Shanks said in a statement.

He described the generator as "tiny" but said his department had briefed CEOs following the intrusion on "steps they should take to stay secure."

WATER CYBERATTACK HITS AT LEAST 7 STATES

The British shutdown came weeks after hackers struck more than 30 community water systems in Minnesota, accessing technology used to remotely monitor and control pumps and other equipment. Minnesota officials have not publicly attributed the attacks. Several news outlets, citing U.S. officials and a leaked industry threat-sharing memo, reported that Iran was the likely culprit. President Donald Trump has publicly rejected that assessment, saying he did not believe Iran was to blame.

Together, the incidents are putting civilian infrastructure at the center of another front in the conflict between the U.S. and Iran. As the military confrontation stretches into its sixth month, relatively small and often lightly defended water and energy facilities offer hackers a way to cause physical disruption without penetrating a major power grid or striking a military target.

Those facilities can be especially vulnerable because many rely on internet-connected industrial control systems that allow operators to monitor and manage physical equipment remotely. Once inside, hackers can interrupt operations, lock out operators or manipulate controls for pumps and other machinery.

In a July alert, the FBI and Environmental Protection Agency said malicious actors had targeted water and wastewater utilities in at least seven states by accessing exposed programmable logic controllers and changing their internet addresses and passwords. Some incidents disrupted water operations, causing reported pressure loss and flooding.

Federal agencies have also warned that Iranian-affiliated actors have targeted similar industrial devices across water, energy and government sectors, seeking access to the software used to control them. That activity has already caused operational disruptions and financial losses.

IRAN’S PROXY WAR HAS CROSSED OCEANS AND IS NOW KNOCKING ON AMERICA’S DOOR

Iranian hackers have pursued U.S. infrastructure before.

The threat extends beyond industrial systems. On Aug. 18, the Justice Department charged 17 members of an Iran-based company with carrying out a sweeping cyber theft campaign targeting hundreds of universities, private companies and government agencies. Prosecutors said many of the intrusions were conducted on behalf of the IRGC and other Iranian entities and resulted in the theft of more than 31 terabytes of academic data and intellectual property.

In 2016, the Justice Department charged an Iranian hacker with gaining access to the control system for a dam in Rye, New York. The dam’s sluice gate had been disconnected for maintenance at the time, preventing him from manipulating water levels and flow rates.

More recently, U.S. agencies linked an IRGC-affiliated campaign known as CyberAv3ngers to compromises of Israeli-made industrial controllers at dozens of U.S. facilities in late 2023 and early 2024, including water and wastewater systems, energy companies, food manufacturers and healthcare organizations. The campaign exploited devices exposed to the public internet that were still using default passwords.

The more recent attacks underscore how little access may be required to produce a physical effect. In Minnesota, compromised controllers affected systems used to track water levels, pressure, pump operations and equipment alarms; in some communities, equipment was temporarily taken offline while operators restored systems.

Whether Tehran intends a wider campaign against Western infrastructure remains unclear. But the four-day shutdown in Britain illustrates what hackers can do once they gain access to a small industrial system: disrupt physical operations without breaching a major grid operator or triggering a blackout large enough to invite an immediate military response.

item.title: Phillies vs Mariners player props and over under picks as Philadelphia eyes 10th consecutive win
item.description: Zack Wheeler faces Logan Gilbert as the Philadelphia Phillies ride a nine-game win streak against the struggling Seattle Mariners in a key matchup.
item.content:encoded:
Baseball tends to be a season full of streaks from teams. Some months, teams are awesome; some months they stink. It is easier to notice the successes or failures of teams when they are earlier in the season. You can see when a team is struggling more easily when their record is 11-16 as opposed to 55-59, for example. What happens when one of the hottest teams in baseball takes on one of the coldest teams? That's what we have tonight as the Phillies play the Mariners.

The Philadelphia Phillies are one of the hottest teams in baseball, having won their ninth straight game yesterday on a walk-off homer. It was a bit of a miraculous comeback as the Phillies were down 4-0 before the team scored six in the bottom of the ninth to win it. The team has won 16 of their past 21 games and is now threatening to take over the Braves for the best team in the National League East. It is fairly unlikely that they would miss the postseason, but that wasn't something that could be said before this stretch. On July 31, they were just four games above .500 and looking like the team that started the season instead of the one that had a great turnaround.

Today the team sends out one of their aces, giving them a good chance to make it to 10 wins in a row as Zack Wheeler takes the hill. Wheeler takes the ball today with a 10-4 record, 2.92 ERA, and a 1.01 WHIP. He has also racked up 144 strikeouts. He has been solid on the road this campaign with a slightly lower ERA at 2.67. This has been the worst month of his season, though. In August, he has allowed 10 earned runs over 17.1 innings of work. He hasn't completed six innings in any of his last five outings. Wheeler has been good against the Mariners in the past, holding them to a .172 batting average.

PHILLIES SEND CY YOUNG CONTENDER CHRISTOPHER SANCHEZ TO THE MOUND IN WILD CARD RACE SHOWDOWN

The Seattle Mariners are one of the most frustrating teams in baseball. They are seven games under .500 this season, despite looking like one of the best teams in baseball, at least on paper. Somehow, the team is under .500 and in jeopardy of missing the postseason. They are currently three games behind the Rangers and Astros, who are currently tied for first. It doesn't help that they also have to battle the Orioles, Twins, Blue Jays, and Guardians for the final Wild Card spot. They are also three games back in that race, and the Tigers are just behind at 3.5 games.

Looking to battle the Phillies and Wheeler is Logan Gilbert. For the season, Gilbert is 10-7 with a 3.35 ERA and a 1.01 WHIP. The problem that Gilbert has is that he has pitched much worse at home this season than on the road. He has allowed 20 homers this season, and 18 of them have come in Seattle. His road ERA is a stellar 2.49, but his home ERA is all the way up there at 4.01. He doesn't give up too many runs in the majority of starts, but this is not a place you'd want to trust him.

One guy that stands out for us to fade tonight is Randy Arozarena of the Mariners. For his career, he is just 1-for-13 against Wheeler with seven strikeouts. I'll take the under on his hits for tonight. Brandon Marsh of the Phillies is another one that might be worth fading tonight. He is just 2-for-17 against Gilbert with six strikeouts. I'm taking his under on hits tonight as well.

Aside from those plus-money props we have on the card, I've got a play for the game. The total is just 6.5 tonight, which is absurd to me. Gilbert allows runs on the road, and I think we should see the Phillies score three or four at least tonight. I'll take a shot on the over. I also think the Phillies will win this game tonight. The line is moving toward the Mariners, but Gilbert has shown he allows homers at home, and Wheeler has been great. Give me the over, Phillies, and the two player props.

item.title: Trump wants cheaper beef. Republicans in key races warn his plan goes too far
item.description: Senate Republicans, including Tom Cotton and Tim Sheehy, push back on Trump's plan to import 300,000 metric tons of foreign ground beef to lower prices.
item.content:encoded:
Senate Republicans racing to keep their grip on power have beef with President Donald Trump’s latest affordability push.

A handful of Republicans in the upper chamber aren’t happy with Trump’s directive to allow hundreds of thousands of tons of foreign beef into the U.S. in a bid to lower grocery bills. It comes as Americans’ struggles with everyday affordability have erupted as a key issue for voters across the country.

Sen. Tom Cotton, R-Ark., who is up for re-election this cycle and is one of Trump’s top allies in the Senate, argued that beef prices are high "for a simple reason: Our cattle herd is too small."

TRUMP URGED TO STOP TARGETING FELLOW REPUBLICANS AS GOP FIGHTS TO KEEP MAJORITY

"Imported beef below market prices will only put more pressure on our cattlemen," Cotton said on X. "I have advised the President against this ill-advised action in the past and I now urge him to reconsider. We need to support our cattlemen, grow the herd, and let the market work."

Trump last week announced on Truth Social his intent to flood the market with 300,000 metric tons of imported ground beef with a commitment that the product would be sold at 25% below current market prices over a 90-day span.

It comes as ground beef prices have soared to roughly $7 per pound, while the nation’s cattle herd earlier this year hit historic lows not seen since the 1950s, according to data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA).

TOP GOP GROUP PUMPS $37M INTO FIGHT ON KEY ISSUE DOMINATING MIDTERM RACES: 'MUCH MORE TO COME'

Trump defended his import plan as he headed to South Carolina to stump for Sen. Darline Graham, R-S.C., arguing "that’s what the people want."

"That’s what the voters want, and that’s what I want. The ranchers are great. They’re my people. I love the ranchers," Trump said. "They’ve done a fantastic job, but they admit that we need a little help in order to get the prices down, so that’s what we’re doing."

Neither Trump, nor the administration, has so far said which countries the ground beef would come from. But earlier this year, he signed an executive order similarly aimed at lowering beef prices by allowing an influx of 80,000 metric tons of beef trimmings from Argentina.

Republicans at the time privately fumed over the directive in a closed-door meeting in the Senate with Vice President JD Vance.

And now, Republicans running for office in America’s heartland again disagree.

"I want to lower prices, but this is a bad idea," Rep. Ashley Hinson, R-Iowa, said on X.

SENATE MAP TIGHTENS AS TOP FORECASTER MOVES 3 RACES TOWARD DEMOCRATS

Hinson is running in one of the tightest races in the country to replace retiring Sen. Joni Ernst, R-Iowa. Cook Political Report rated the race a toss-up last week.

Other in-cycle incumbents aren’t thrilled with Trump’s push, either. Sen. Mike Rounds, R-S.D., charged, "This Hurts!," while Sen. Pete Ricketts, R-Neb., contended that he appreciated the work to "lower grocery prices," but warned that "short-term policy shifts do not equal long-term solutions."

"Flooding the market with lower quality beef compromises Nebraska farmers and ranchers," Ricketts said.

Trump’s other key Senate allies aren’t thrilled with the plan either.

Sen. Tim Sheehy, R-Mont., said he’s advised Trump not to do this for the last year because it would harm American ranchers, "most of whom are MAGA Republicans."

"The president’s heart is in the right place on wanting lower prices for the American people, and beef prices have been impacted by the Mexican screwworm," Sheehy said.

The White House and the USDA did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

item.title: WNBA fight over males in women's sports exposes how the left keeps answering a question nobody asked
item.description: Natasha Cloud said trans people "belong" after confronting Enes Kanter Freedom, but the WNBA still hasn't answered the real eligibility question.
item.content:encoded:
WNBA player Natasha Cloud had a message for transgender people Sunday night.

The Chicago Sky guard wrote on social media that trans people "belong," that they're loved, seen and "perfect as you are." She added that they would always be "protected" by her.

WNBA HAS 'NO IDEA WHAT THEY'RE ABOUT TO FACE,' ENES KANTER FREEDOM SAYS AS LEAGUE TAKES ON TRANS ATHLETE ISSUE

It came after Cloud confronted Enes Kanter Freedom during the Sky's 113-90 loss to the Indiana Fever at Wintrust Arena on Sunday night. Freedom has spent the past few weeks pushing the WNBA on something that really shouldn't be difficult to answer: Can a male play in a women's professional basketball league?

Cloud answered a question nobody asked.

The fight isn't over who gets through the doors at a WNBA arena. Freedom is asking whether a male is allowed to play in a women's league. Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham has made the same basic point, saying "biological men" shouldn't compete in women's sports.

But there's a reason the conversation keeps getting dragged somewhere else: defending males in women's sports is a much harder argument to make than simply declaring "trans people belong."

And Cloud wasn't the only one doing this over the weekend.

The New York Liberty hosted the Fever at Barclays Center on Saturday, and the scoreboard featured messages specifically welcoming transgender fans.

"Welcome Trans Liberty fans! You are loved and you belong!" one read.

Another said, "Hey trans fans! Glad you're here! Go Liberty!"

WOMAN CLAIMS NY LIBERTY TRIED TO CHANGE HER 'XX-XY' PAID SCOREBOARD MESSAGE FOR HALFTIME OF FEVER GAME

Outside the arena, transgender activists showed up to counter a rally supporting Cunningham and chanted "trans lives matter."

Okay. Sure.

Transgender fans are welcome at basketball games. Treat them like everyone else in the building.

Now, can we talk about the actual issue?

Because the response to Cunningham is a perfect example of what’s been happening in this debate for years.

Back in 2023, USA Today columnist Nancy Armour went after ESPN's Sam Ponder for supporting fairness in women's sports.

Armour called Ponder's position "bigotry" and accused Riley Gaines and others fighting to keep males out of women's sports of promoting hate.

I wrote at the time that Gaines wasn't "anti-trans." She was pro-woman.

Gaines' position has always been that the women's category should be reserved for females. You can disagree with her, but at least disagree with what she's actually saying.

Calling her a bigot or a transphobe is much easier than explaining why she's wrong.

A few months later, I went to Harvard when Riley Gaines spoke on campus. Before she even arrived, a Harvard athletic administrator had described her as an "athlete-turned-anti-trans-activist."

Sound familiar?

Rather than explain why Gaines was wrong about women's sports, the administrator branded her "anti-trans."

Then Martina Navratilova got the same treatment.

Navratilova has been one of the most outspoken female athletes in the country on this issue. She thinks women's sports should be for females.

A tennis reporter called her "transphobic" and accused her of going on an "anti-trans crusade."

So explain why Navratilova is wrong.

Seriously. Explain why a male should be entitled to compete in a female athletic category. That's the hard part, so critics change the subject to hate, safety or claims that children struggling with gender identity need to be "protected."

And now the WNBA is doing its own version of the same thing.

For years, the playbook was simple: call anyone who objected a bigot or a transphobe.

Now the tactic is a little different. Don't defend males in women's sports. Just announce how much you love transgender people.

Minnesota Lynx coach Cheryl Reeve wore a "Trans Kids Belong" shirt after Cunningham's comments started getting attention. Then came the Liberty scoreboard. Then Cloud's post.

But Cunningham wasn't talking about whether some kid somewhere feels like he or she "belongs."

"Trans Kids Belong" is a slogan, not an argument. And slogans become pretty useful when the logic isn't on your side. It still doesn't answer whether a male is eligible to play in the WNBA.

Freedom has forced the WNBA to confront that question.

He has publicly said he intends to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft. Former NBA player Royce White has said the same. Obviously, they're making a point, and it's a useful one because the WNBA's own publicly cited eligibility language says only players who are women can play, but the league has not publicly defined the term.

So define "woman," WNBA. That shouldn't take multiple meetings over "weeks and months." The WNBA exists for female basketball players, which should mean a male isn't eligible.

Period.

And every time the question comes up, the WNBA drags the discussion back to hate, inclusion and protecting transgender people. Pretty soon we're miles away from the reason anyone started talking about this in the first place.

A trans fan can go to a Liberty game, buy a jersey and spend the night yelling at the refs like everyone else. Nobody's debating whether that person gets to sit in the stands.

We're talking about who gets to be on the court.

Women's sports exist because sex matters in athletic competition. That's why female athletes have their own leagues, divisions and championships in the first place.

So protect that category.

Keeping males out of women's sports isn't a statement about how anyone should be treated outside of sports.

Cloud can post whatever message she wants, and the Liberty can welcome trans fans on the scoreboard. Fine.

But the WNBA still hasn't answered the question that started this whole debate.

Should a male be allowed to compete in women's sports?

No.

Maybe someday the people calling everyone else hateful will explain why they think the answer should be yes.

item.title: 49ers owner Jed York arrested for 'engaging in prostitution' in Ohio, pleads no contest to lesser charges
item.description: Jed York pleaded no contest to disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools charges in East Palestine, Ohio, and now faces NFL discipline.
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco 49ers owner and CEO John "Jed" York was arrested and arraigned in East Palestine, Ohio on suspicion of "engaging in prostitution" and "possessing criminal tools" charges that were later amended to misdemeanor charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools, according to court records.

York was booked Sunday morning and released that afternoon on a $5,000 bond, the Columbiana County Sheriff’s Office confirmed to OutKick.

The arrest occurred at the Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community – a trailer park.

East Palestine police referred OutKick to contact the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force for more information. The Task Force has not responded to a request for comment.

York appeared in Columbiana County Municipal Court on Monday morning. He pleaded no contest to the two misdemeanor charges after the prosecutor filed a plea agreement. 

He must serve two days in jail, with one of those already credited for time served.

BRANDON AIYUK DROVE 104 MPH NEAR LEVI'S STADIUM AND FILMED IT, NOW A WARRANT HAS BEEN ISSUED FOR HIS ARREST

York was also ordered to pay $1,150 in fines.

York, 46, will be subject to NFL discipline under the Personal Conduct Policy.

"We are aware of the matter which will be reviewed under the personal conduct policy," the NFL told OutKick in a statement.

The 49ers, meanwhile, are not looking to make this story any more attention-grabbing.

"As this is a legal matter which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time," the club said in a statement.

York has been the majority owner of the 49ers since 2024 and was previously the team's CEO. He is originally from Youngstown, Ohio.

item.title: Jeffries' reported meeting with Kushner about possible Trump cooperation draws left-wing backlash
item.description: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, a New York Democrat, met with President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, reports indicate.
item.content:encoded:
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., and President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner met in recent weeks and spoke about possible issues of common ground, according to reports, landing the top House Democrat in hot water with some on the political left who have taken issue with the reported get-together.

The men talked about housing, immigration and high living costs as possible categories of common ground, the New York Times reported. Kushner, the husband of Trump's daughter Ivanka, suggested that the lawmaker should meet with White House chief of staff Susie Wiles, two individuals with knowledge of the meet-up noted, according to the outlet.

Fox News Digital reached out to Jeffries' offices and the White House on Monday.

KUSHNER GIVES HAMAS STARK ULTIMATUM: DISARM OR ISRAEL GETS US BACKING TO 'FINISH THE JOB'

"Throughout this Congress, Republicans have adopted a my-way-or-the-highway approach to governing that has failed the American people. To stop the madness, we have repeatedly made clear that an extremist approach will not work and will be met with forceful opposition," Jeffries said in a statement obtained by Fox News Digital.

"The American people want bold change and that’s what House Democrats will deliver. In every conversation that we have with the Trump administration, we will continue to make it explicitly clear that the affordability crisis is not a hoax and nothing short of transformational policy change is acceptable. We are fighting for an affordable America. The question is whether Republicans will join us," he said in the statement.

Some on the left have objected to the reported meeting between the congressman and Kushner.

SOCIALISM SURGES AMONG DEMOCRATS AS PARTY LEADERS REJECT DSA AGENDA: 'PACK OF FOOLS'

Zeteo founder, CEO and editor-in-chief Mehdi Hasan declared in a post on X, "The only meeting Hakeem Jeffries should be having with Jared Kushner is to tell him he’ll be subpoenaed by the House for a corruption investigation on day one of Democratic control of the House. This is just pathetic stuff from the House Dem leader."

Michelle Kinney, co-founder of The Mayday Network, wrote on X, "They should be f[---]ing hauling Jared Kushner in front of a committee, not MEETING with him. What in the absolute f--- WE ARE ALL SO SICK OF THIS S--- — ENOUGH!!!!"

Dean Obeidallah wrote on "The Dean's Report": "How could Jeffries not know the meeting would get leaked and it was the wrong thing to do?! This meeting doesn’t help Democrats win in November. In fact, now that we know about it, the result has been many Democrats slamming Jeffries online while some still defend him—causing a distraction to our real goal."

MIKE JOHNSON TAUNTS HAKEEM JEFFRIES FOR LOSING DEMS' CIVIL WAR 'IN HIS OWN BACKYARD'

While Republicans currently hold a slight majority in the House of Representatives, Democrats have the opportunity to win the majority in the upcoming midterm elections.

If Democrats manage to flip control of the House, Jeffries would be a prime candidate for speaker.

item.title: Hayden Panettiere’s mom discloses heartbreaking ultimatum in their final phone call before actress’ death
item.description: Hayden Panettiere's mom reveals the therapist-advised ultimatum over Brian Hickerson that led to their estrangement months before the actress' death.
item.content:encoded:
Hayden Panettiere's mom is detailing the heartbreaking ultimatum that led to their estrangement months before the actress' death.

In an interview with "Good Morning America," which aired Monday, Lesley Vogel said she and the late actress had become estranged in the months before Panettiere's death after Vogel gave her daughter an ultimatum over her daughter's relationship with on-again, off-again boyfriend Brian Hickerson.

About a year ago, Vogel traveled to California to stay with Panettiere and help her end her relationship with Hickerson — a decision the "Nashville" star made on her own, Vogel claimed.

HAYDEN PANETTIERE'S MOTHER POINTS FINGER AT BRIAN HICKERSON AFTER 'NASHVILLE' STAR'S DEATH AT 36

"She knew that Brian was toxic," Vogel said. "She knew she had to get him out of her life."

Vogel said things began to change after about six weeks, when she noticed her daughter slowly pulling away. It was then that she returned home to Florida.

HAYDEN PANETTIERE AND THE CHILD STARS WHOSE RELATIONSHIPS WITH THEIR MOMAGERS TURNED COMPLICATED

"When I got the phone call from her saying, ‘I’m going to be with the person I love,’ … I just lost it," Vogel recalled. "I could not believe that she had gone that far back, that he had been successful in reeling her back in with all of the things he had done to her."

Vogel said that, on the advice of her therapist, she told Panettiere that she could no longer speak with her as long as Hickerson remained part of her life.

The decision marked the beginning of their estrangement — something Vogel believed would only be temporary.

"I needed to have that pocket of time," she said. "Of course, I thought it was going to be a pocket of time. I did not by any stretch of the imagination think that this was going to happen to Hayden."

"I don’t know why, I just didn’t," she added. "Maybe I didn’t want to."

Panettiere was found dead inside a Greenville, South Carolina residence on Aug. 16.

POLICE SHOW UP AT HOME LINKED TO HAYDEN PANETTIERE’S ON-AND-OFF BOYFRIEND DAYS AFTER HER SUDDEN DEATH

Hickerson and his brother, Zach, called 911 after finding the actress unresponsive, according to a police report obtained by Fox News Digital. Hickerson later gave authorities a bag containing medication Panettiere had been taking, according to the report.

Fox News has learned the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) has also been contacted and is assisting with the investigation.

DISNEY ALUM CHRISTY CARLSON ROMANO RIPS HOLLYWOOD FOR FAILING CHILD STARS AFTER HAYDEN PANETTIERE’S DEATH

"I would say at about 17, I started seeing her going downhill," Vogel said. "As she got older, and it wasn’t my voice anymore. I wasn’t in charge of her choices."

Panettiere's decision to give up custody of her daughter, Kaya — whom she shared with former fiancé Wladimir Klitschko — was a turning point, Vogel said.

"Vlad had taken over custody, you know, for safety," Vogel said. "In my opinion, that was the catalyst that she just couldn’t keep those demons away."

In an interview with the New York Times, Vogel said her daughter was living with chronic physical pain.

"She was in pain," Vogel said. "She was afraid. She couldn’t physically function properly."

Now that doesn't make sense because when you look at a beautiful girl who's got an incredible career, even though it has had its ups and downs, but, you look at that big picture, and you go, 'Why would you be suffering?' People don't understand that you can have, on the exterior, all of this, but that doesn't mean that what's going on in here matches."

item.title: Mamdani jumps into Democratic Party feud, alleging boss seeking to subvert 'will of voters'
item.description: Zohran Mamdani opposes Rodneyse Bichotte Hermelyn's push to add voting members to the Brooklyn Democratic Party executive committee before a fall vote.
item.content:encoded:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is opposing a last-minute push to overhaul Brooklyn Democratic Party rules, arguing the proposed changes would undermine voters after reformers made gains in the June primary.

"I very much oppose these proposed changes, by the current Brooklyn Democratic Party chair," Mamdani said. "I oppose them because they are an attempt to circumnavigate the will of voters."

The proposals from Brooklyn Democratic Party chair Rodneyse Bichotte Hermelyn would add more than two dozen voting members to the party’s executive committee, which will choose the party chair this fall, after a slate of reformers won 22 district leader seats in the June primary, according to the City Reporter.

NYC TAXPAYERS COULD PAY TWICE UNDER MAMDANI'S CITY-OWNED GROCERY STORE PLAN

The newly elected district leaders will not take their seats until the fall, and Bichotte Hermelyn and her supporters still hold a majority as current district leaders prepare to vote on the proposed changes Tuesday night, according to the outlet.

Bichotte Hermelyn has described the changes as an effort to broaden participation in the party.

"We want to create a perception of inclusiveness," she told NY1. In a video released by the Brooklyn Democratic organization, she said the proposals would "expand leadership" and "expand representation."

The reformers have backed longtime Sunset Park district leader Julio Peña to become the next party chair. If the proposed changes pass, the additional voting members would take part in the fall leadership election.

VICE PRESIDENT JD VANCE BLASTS MAMDANI, EL-SAYED, AOC AND OSSOFF IN RAPID-FIRE TIKTOK ROAST

Mamdani said the Brooklyn Democratic Party should reflect what New Yorkers want, rather than the kind of politics that has left people "disengaged and disaffected with politics at large."

New York Attorney General Letitia James and Public Advocate Jumaane Williams have also urged the party not to move forward with the changes.

"New Yorkers deserve leaders who are committed to serving their communities, not rewriting rules to hold onto power," they said in a joint statement obtained by City and State New York. "Changing the makeup of an executive committee on the eve of a leadership vote goes against what we believe in as Democrats and should not move forward."

Another proposal would give former party chairs a vote in future leadership elections even after they are no longer district leaders.

According to the City Reporter, that appears to mean former party chair Clarence Norman could vote on future party leadership. Norman resigned in 2005 after multiple corruption convictions, including one for soliciting bribes from judicial nominees.

After the leadership election, another proposed change would allow additional voting members to be appointed from each Assembly district, potentially bringing the executive committee to about 90 members.

item.title: Reporter's Notebook: College sports bill enters legislative 'red zone' as season kicks off
item.description: As North Carolina and Texas Christian open the season in Dublin, the Senate's bipartisan college sports bill stalls amid disputes over NIL rules.
item.content:encoded:
The college football season kicks off this Saturday with North Carolina playing Texas Christian University in Dublin, Ireland.

This marks the start of a sprint until early April when college football and basketball practically compete on a near-daily basis with MLB, the NFL, the NBA and NHL.

This college football season begins with lawmakers falling short of a goal to pass a bill to alter the flow of money in college sports. And despite recent momentum, lawmakers may be lucky to pass the bill when the clock shows zeroes on April 5 in Detroit and the NCAA crowns its next basketball Final Four champion.

PROTECT COLLEGE SPORTS ACT STALLS IN OVERNIGHT SENATE SHOWDOWN, VOTE PUSHED TO SEPTEMBER AFTER CHAOTIC EVENING

President Trump demanded that the Senate stay in session this month to pass a bipartisan college sports measure. That wasn’t going to happen simply because the bill’s not ready yet. The measure didn’t even secure a specific agreement for a test vote when the Senate returns in September. Senate Commerce Committee Chairman Ted Cruz, R-Texas, said there was a deal for a vote at some point. However, an unrelated bill to regulate cryptocurrency marshaled a concrete time for a test vote on the afternoon of Tuesday, Sept. 15. The college sports measure didn’t head into the August recess with that level of certainty.

But the one thing that is certain? Intercollegiate athletics face myriad problems.

"College sports right now is in crisis. It is chaos that is ripping college sports apart," said Cruz.

"I think that the arms race that exists now where people are just paying any amount of money from a system is not the right way to get this done," said Sen. Maria Cantwell, D-Wash. She’s the top Democrat on the Senate Commerce Committee and helped craft the bipartisan legislation with Cruz.

CLOCK IS TICKING AS SENATORS TED CRUZ, MARIA CANTWELL PUSH FOR SEC, BIG TEN BUY-IN ON COLLEGE SPORTS BILL

The measure establishes a national standard for athlete compensation — including NIL — for the use of name, image and likeness of athletes. It also limits them to one transfer without losing eligibility within a five-year window.

But understanding the bill’s remedies is challenging.

"[The bill] seemed pretty dense when I read it," yours truly observed to Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., one afternoon in a hallway of the Dirksen Senate Office Building.

"It's dense as hell," replied Kennedy. "And that’s a legal term."

The measure raises the ceiling of money schools can use to compensate athletes. It essentially allows "third-party entities," like athletic footwear or equipment manufacturers like Under Armour or Nike, to pipeline additional money to schools.

Naturally, football and men’s basketball score most of the money under the current system. But lawmakers worry that women’s athletics and smaller sports like volleyball, lacrosse and soccer could evaporate unless Congress intervenes.

"It's the revenue from football and maybe basketball, but mostly football that funds everything else," said Sen. Chris Coons, D-Del.

The college sports bill seemed to gain traction in late July when the Big Ten and SEC — the most muscular of all college athletic conferences — announced their support of the legislation. Lawmakers could try to write a bill all they wanted, but with all due respect to the Mid-American Conference and Mountain West, the measure wouldn’t go anywhere unless the Big Ten and SEC were on board.

It was thought that the college sports package might get a test vote before the August recess, but a band of conservatives claimed the legislation fell short when it came to protecting women from competing against men.

"It looks like a bunch of trial lawyers drew this thing up," said Sen. Tommy Tuberville, R-Ala., a former Division I football coach who ran programs at Ole Miss, Auburn, Texas Tech and Cincinnati.

UNIVERSITIES ARE DESPERATE TO WIN NOW, BUT ATHLETES AND THE NATION BOTH LOSE

Tuberville teamed up with Sens. Jim Banks, R-Ind., and Josh Hawley, R-Mo., to craft an amendment going further in the legislation. Banks believed that the bill could undercut Indiana state law, which extends prohibitions on biological males competing in K-12 sports to college athletics. Banks expressed concern that the Cruz/Cantwell bill "would preempt Indiana’s law." The Indiana Republican asserted that he couldn’t support the legislation as written.

However, President Donald Trump torched those who said the bill failed to bar men from playing women’s sports at any level.

"Nobody has done more to protect Women Athletes than me — and this Bill CLEARLY protects the Laws in 27 States protecting Women's Sports, and banning Men from Women's Sports. Anyone who tells you differently is LYING!" thundered the president on Truth Social.

Trump worried that without adoption of this legislation, "Programs will be canceled, Women's and Olympic Sports will go away, the fans will be robbed, and Universities will go broke." He then asked the Senate to "stay in D.C. until it passes."

Despite the president’s advocacy, that wasn’t going to happen. However, the legislation does have a new set of downs — thanks to the Big Ten and SEC.

The Congressional Black Caucus (CBC) opposes the bill. In a statement, the CBC said the package fails to incorporate "perspectives of Black athletes."

Sen. Cory Booker, D-N.J., is the only former Division I football player in the Senate, competing as a tight end for Stanford. He opposes the bill.

"There are a lot of people who have substantive objections with that bill that should give us all pause," said Booker.

THE "PROTECT COLLEGE SPORTS ACT" HAS A FATAL FLAW: IT DOESN’T PROTECT WOMEN | RILEY GAINES

So the Senate essentially took a timeout on the bill with the August recess. As any fan knows, timeouts are essential in sports. They allow teams to regroup. Rehydrate with water or Gatorade. Players to catch their breath. Coaches to draw up a special play to bring the team to victory.

It’s not known what the play call might be from Cruz, Cantwell or even Trump. Or if anything would work. Some skeptics believe the Senate’s decision to leave Washington without the locked-in test vote could cost the bill momentum — compared to the deal dictating the test vote on the cryptocurrency legislation.

The University of Oklahoma led the nation in red-zone efficiency last season. The Sooners scored touchdowns more than 97% of the time when moving the ball within 20 yards of the end zone.

Ninety-seven percent is a ridiculously efficient figure. The Philadelphia Eagles were the NFL’s best red zone team last season, scoring touchdowns around 70% of the time.

The U.S. Senate is not the gridiron. But it’s clear that the bill to regulate college sports has now entered the legislative red zone. A lot of legislation gets this close to the goal line, but senators rarely enjoy the success of the Sooners or Eagles when it comes to punching it in.

That’s why it’s possible that this legislative drive could stall — despite a steady march down the field.

item.title: John Cusack stands in 'solidarity' with Mark Ruffalo amid Paramount's antisemitism allegation
item.description: John Cusack backed Mark Ruffalo after Paramount accused the actor of invoking antisemitic tropes in his criticism of Oracle's ties to the Israeli military.
item.content:encoded:
Actor John Cusack threw his support behind fellow Hollywood star Mark Ruffalo over the weekend as Ruffalo pushed back against Paramount's accusations that his criticism of tech giant Oracle invoked "antisemitic tropes."

"Solidarity — well said." Cusack wrote on X in response to Ruffalo’s lengthy defense of his remarks, which centered on Oracle’s ties to the Israeli military and the company’s leadership.

The controversy erupted after Ruffalo criticized Oracle executive vice chair Safra Catz, who also sits on Paramount’s board, and reposted a video of her discussing "really profoundly scary technologies" Oracle used to assist the Israeli military following the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas terror attacks.

CNN STAFFERS BRACE FOR PARAMOUNT CEO'S POTENTIAL PLAN TO LAUNCH EDITORIAL BOARD TO OVERSEE NETWORK

Ruffalo tied his criticism of Oracle to the Ellison family's proposed $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, pointing to Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison and his son, Paramount CEO David Ellison. The actor argued that the deal, which would put CNN, HBO and Warner Bros. under the same family's control, raises concerns about editorial independence, jobs and more.

"These 'really profoundly scary technologies' will most likely be merged into one of the largest media conglomerates in the world and one day used on you. Look how she revels in what we now have come to see as a genocide, which was built on an apartheid system of oppression powered by Oracle," the Marvel actor wrote in an Instagram story.

HASAN PIKER STANDS BY 'INTENTIONALLY PROVOCATIVE' CLAIMS THAT HAMAS IS 'A THOUSAND TIMES BETTER' THAN ISRAEL

Paramount subsequently issued a statement saying it was "troubled when antisemitic tropes are invoked" in what it characterized as a business dispute.

"Words like ‘genocide’ and ‘apartheid,’ applied to a corporate transaction, aren’t just wrong. They’re a bridge too far, and they cheapen the very real suffering those words are meant to describe," a company spokesperson added.

Ruffalo fired back Saturday, telling Fox News Digital the accusation that he is antisemitic was "appalling and fundamentally dishonest." He maintained that criticism of the Israeli government, military technology contracts or the executives behind them should not be equated with criticism of Jewish people.

"Scrutinizing the Ellisons, including Oracle’s business built on data, surveillance technology and government contracts and the serious threat to editorial freedom and the loss of a livelihood for thousands of families, is fair and necessary," he said.

CALIFORNIA AG ROB BONTA FACES ‘POLITICAL FAVOR’ CLAIMS OVER NETFLIX-LINKED $1M TRAIL IN PARAMOUNT SUIT

"The $111 billion deal would hand one family control over CNN, HBO and Warner Bros., backed in part by foreign money whose influence on editorial decisions has never been fully explained to the public."

"Lawmakers on both sides of the aisle have called for serious national security review, and regulators still haven’t given the public a real answer. Until they do, the merger shouldn’t move forward. Now is the time to dive boldly into all these issues, not step back or concede," he added.

The potential merger has also drawn legal scrutiny from a coalition of 12 state attorneys general challenging the deal. Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery have agreed not to close the transaction until five days after a court rules on the merits of the states’ claims or June 1, 2027, whichever comes first.

In a statement noted by The Hollywood Reporter, Simon Wiesenthal Center CEO Jim Berk said, "Words matter, and so does the willingness to draw a line when legitimate debate gives way to antisemitic tropes. We commend Paramount for speaking clearly and refusing to allow prejudice to masquerade as political or corporate criticism."

Film critic Christian Toto, the founder and editor of Hollywood in Toto, told Fox News, "I'm guessing Mark would rather John Cusack have stayed silent on the matter!" Toto then pointed to controversial comments that Cusack has made on the situation in the Middle East. 

Toto continued, "More importantly, the issue in play is getting more attention now that antisemitism is flaring up in the culture at large and within the Democratic Party. That hasn't bled into Hollywood, Inc., yet, but it might sooner than later. Maybe a good example of that fracture is happening with the Paramount merger fight. Some Hollywood groups and Democrats are requesting a resolution to the matter, while others have dug their heels in, battling the merger at all costs."

He concluded, "This could get ugly, becoming a Blue on Blue battle within La La Land that could cause real damage to careers."

item.title: Mustafa Ali survives Jason Hotch's OMG moment to retain TNA International Championship
item.description: Mustafa Ali recaptured the TNA International Championship at TNA Lockdown with a 450 splash, but Jason Hotch's crossbody off the cage stole the show.
item.content:encoded:

Even as Ali won, Hotch may have had the moment of the night.
